# What this host's A/A noise has measured

`δ` is an **A/A** spread (`docs/PHASE1.md` §9): the largest slowdown the paired-bootstrap
95% CI reaches when the *same* code is run against itself, so it is this machine and never
a change. Measured, never asserted.

**This file is a log, not the gate's allowance.** §9 records `δ` here and `--against`
deliberately does not read it, because on this host the number does not survive the walk
from one session to the next — see the table. The allowance `--against` uses is a control
measured beside the comparison, in the same invocation, on the same benchmark
(`0033`, draft). What this log is for: knowing whether the machine is quiet enough to bother.

Last measured: **0.0707 (7.07%)** worst, over 1 recorded run(s).

| run | benchmarks | median `δ` | max `δ` | CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 60 | 0.0031 | 0.0707 | AMD EPYC-Milan Processor, 8 logical CPUs |

**A stored floor does not reproduce, and the spread is not subtle.** Two sessions a few
hours apart, same protocol, same binary against itself: worst `δ` 0.0161, then 0.6864; p75
0.0036, then 0.0832; 0 of 60 benchmarks above 2%, then 23. A floor from the quiet session
fails the identical binary against itself, and one from the noisy session would pass a 50%
regression. Nothing in the protocol changed between them; the machine's state did, and a
shared VM does not announce that (`available_parallelism` read 1 at one bless and 8 at
another).

**Neither one floor per benchmark nor an accumulated maximum survives that.** Per
benchmark was measured first: across two quiet sessions the *distribution* over the 60
reproduces (min 0.0008 then 0.0009, median 0.0029 then 0.0030) while single benchmarks do
not — `exp_coeffs_straddle-0.9` read 0.0019, then 0.0190 — and 8 of 60 then failed the
identical binary. Accumulating the maximum over runs instead was refuted by the first run
after it: one noisy session pins the allowance at 68% permanently. The per-benchmark table
below is evidence of where the noise is, and is not a set of floors.

**The statistic is the ratio of medians, from the least disturbed of 3 alternations.**
Contamination here is one-sided at both levels — a disturbed sample is slow and never
fast, and so is a disturbed window — so both take a low order statistic. Measured on this
host: one benchmark over eight consecutive windows spread 2.97% by window mean and 1.04%
by window median, while *inside* a window the interquartile spread was 1.1% to 2.7% and
the extremes reached 96%. Taking the mean, then letting a bootstrap resample those extremes
with replacement, gave a worst `δ` of 71.72%; the median gives 1.90% on the same protocol.
Pooling three pairs did not finish the job — a disturbance covering two consecutive runs
puts two of a side's three windows over, past a median's breakdown point, and left one
benchmark at 58.84% where ten consecutive windows of it spread 2.38%. Reporting the
cheapest pair instead survives two disturbed pairs of the three.

**`δ` is `max(high - 1, 1/low - 1)`, not `high - 1`.** Which run of a pair is called the
baseline is a slot name; relabelling replaces the interval by its reciprocal. Taking only
`high` charges a pair for drift one way and nothing for the same drift the other way, and
on this host that gave the four noisiest pairs — 22% to 43% apart — the tightest floors
in the run.

**The two runs of a pair are adjacent in time.** Measured on this host: one benchmark run
four times in a row spreads 0.6%, while the same benchmark measured once per pass of all
60 — the two measurements about two minutes apart — spreads up to 90%. Thermal and
frequency state drift over a pass and do not cancel, and no amount of resampling recovers
it. A floor measured the way the gate measures is the only one that means anything.

Every measurement in every mode runs the bench **binary** directly, built once. One side
under `cargo` and the other direct is not symmetric, and a floor measured both-under-cargo
does not cover it: that asymmetry alone put 3 of 60 identical-code verdicts past their
floor, at 1.007 to 1.018. 1024 resamples. `taskset` is the caller's: the floor is
only as quiet as the machine was.
